title: biomechanics-modality-taxonomy
universal_lens: Modality-specific signal processing frameworks unify biomechanical and kinematic observables via stochastic dynamical systems on embedded manifolds. The sovereign primitive formalizes the hierarchical filtration of biomechanical and health modalities as a constrained measure space. We define a tiered sigma-algebra where higher-fidelity signals (T1) cannot artificially inflate lower-fidelity stochastic processes (T3), enforcing strict orthogonality in the underlying information geometry.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian belief propagation over modalities enables probabilistic inference of athlete load and performance risk using conformal predictive distributions. In GSI, we map these admission gates to a Bayesian hierarchical model with hard truncation priors. A T3 biomechanical posterior is strictly marginalized if combined with a T1 injury report, preventing overconfident conformal prediction intervals from leaking unverified structural assumptions into the final probability distribution.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning in GSE leverages state-transition graphs of player roles and tactical formations informed by positional tracking and video-derived motion patterns. GSE treats modality mixing as a state-transition constraint within a Markov Decision Process. The engine enforces that any composite action value must satisfy independent tier floors for all constituent observations, ensuring situational reasoning does not collapse into spurious correlations during dynamic game-script evaluations.

primitives.name: Physical / Kinetic Modality
primitives.verbatim_quote: --## Modality Registry ### Modality 1 — Physical / Kinetic **What it measures**: Forces, torques, accelerations, joint angles, and movement efficiency in 3D space.
primitives.assumptions: Euclidean spatial framework, rigid body mechanics approximations for skeletal segments.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs at joint angle singularities (e.g., gimbal lock) where angular velocity becomes undefined.

layer2.mapping: The biomechanical measurement of forces and torques maps directly onto the GSI latent state vector as external perturbations, while joint angles serve as state variables for GSE's kinematic state transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Ground Reaction Force (GRF) time-series and joint angle trajectories can be verified via force plate sensors and marker-based motion capture systems.

primitives.name: Radar / Ball-Flight Modality
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Radar / ball-flight**: Trackman, Rapsodo, FlightScope — commercial products with proprietary formats.
primitives.assumptions: Point mass approximation for the ball, linear drag coefficient, constant gravitational acceleration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown occurs when spin dynamics become chaotic (e.g., during high-spin-rate events), violating the point-mass assumption.

layer2.mapping: Radar-derived ball trajectories (position vs. time) serve as empirical priors for GSI's trajectory prediction models, while launch angle and exit velocity inform GSE's situational reasoning about shot outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Ball velocity and spin rate measurements can be cross-verified against high-speed camera data for consistency checks.

primitives.name: Posicional Tracking Modality
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Positional tracking**: Second Spectrum (NBA), Next Gen Stats (NFL), Statcast (MLB), ChyronHego TRACAB (soccer) — all require league program enrollment or commercial license.
primitives.assumptions: Agent tracking accuracy depends on camera calibration and occlusion handling algorithms.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Regime shift happens when multiple agents overlap in the field of view, causing identity switch errors in the tracklet data.

layer2.mapping: Trajectory streams from positional tracking map to GSE's multi-agent state-transition graphs, while pairwise distances inform GSI's conformal prediction regions for opponent positioning.
layer2.telemetry: Average player speed and distance traveled metrics can be validated against wearable IMU data for drift correction.

primitives.name: Video / Computer Vision Modality
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Video / computer vision**: YOLO-based player detection, OpenPose, MediaPipe — open research tools.
primitives.assumptions: Perspective projection model, frame-rate discretization, fixed camera intrinsics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degeneracy occurs when viewpoint changes cause scale ambiguities, leading to misclassification of actions.

layer2.mapping: Object detection confidence scores from video feed map to GSI's belief-state update equations, while pose estimation coordinates parameterize GSE's geometric state space for spatial reasoning.
layer2.telemetry: Action classification accuracy (precision/recall) serves as an empirical metric for validating the robustness of the state-transition model.

primitives.name: Force Plate Kinetic Signature
primitives.verbatim_quote: MTI force plates - Wearable: Catapult GPS, STATSports APEX **Evidence tier ceiling**: T3 (research) / T2 (commercial wearable with license) **Sports OS use case**: Internal context only.
primitives.assumptions: Linear elastic response of force plate transducer; isotropic material properties; quasi-static loading conditions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: T3 research-grade calibration limits; T2 commercial wearables with licensing constraints.

layer2.mapping: GSI inference kernel maps force-time integrals to workload metrics via Gaussian process regression with learned hyperparameters.
layer2.telemetry: Integrated impulse magnitude and temporal duration of ground reaction forces.

primitives.name: Radar-Based Projectile Trajectory
primitives.verbatim_quote: --### Modality 2 — Radar / Ball-Flight **What it measures**: Pitch velocity, spin rate, spin axis, release point, bat speed, exit velocity, launch angle, ball flight trajectory.
primitives.assumptions: Negligible air resistance; constant gravitational acceleration; rigid body approximation of projectile.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ballistic trajectory under uniform gravity; spin-induced Magnus effect requires additional modeling.

layer2.mapping: GSE state-space model encodes radar-derived kinematics as deterministic trajectories within a Markov decision process.
layer2.telemetry: Launch angle, exit velocity, and spin parameters from radar cross-section analysis.

primitives.name: Player Location Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: --### Modality 3 — Positional Tracking **What it measures**: Player locations, speed, acceleration, distance covered, zone entry/exit, formation, spacing metrics.
primitives.assumptions: Smooth motion interpolation between discrete time steps; negligible sensor noise in idealized tracking environment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High-frequency sampling regime; spatial resolution below human perceptual threshold.

layer2.mapping: GSI kernel computes pairwise Euclidean distances and velocity fields across player positions to derive team formation dynamics.
layer2.telemetry: Speed, acceleration, and displacement vectors per player over time windows.

primitives.name: Video Motion Classifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: --### Modality 4 — Video / Computer Vision **What it measures**: Play classification, player movement quality, release mechanics, swing mechanics, tactical pattern recognition.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P(C|I)': 'posterior probability of class C given image I', 'P(I|C)': 'likelihood of image I given class C', 'P(C)': 'prior probability of class C', 'P(I)': 'marginal likelihood of image I'}
primitives.assumptions: Independent and identically distributed observations; sufficient training data for classifier generalization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Deep convolutional neural network classification at frame-level granularity.

layer2.mapping: GSE action recognition module uses video-derived features to map visual inputs into discrete tactical states and transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Action labels, confidence scores, and temporal segmentation of movement sequences.

primitives.name: Independent Tier Floor Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Modality mixing**: When a pick explanation combines signals from multiple modalities, every modality cited must independently meet its tier floor.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Tier Floor: Dimensionless integer classification (T1, T2, T3) representing source fidelity; Pick Explanation: Composite vector of evidence.
primitives.assumptions: Information fusion requires independent validation of each input channel's epistemic reliability before joint inference.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when high-frequency noise from T3 sources is incorrectly whitened by low-frequency T1 signals, creating false precision.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to the GSI Conformal Prediction layer, acting as a hard filter on the nonconformity score aggregation.
layer2.telemetry: Variance reduction ratio between isolated modality predictions and fused ensemble outputs.

primitives.name: Hierarchical Evidence Ceiling
primitives.verbatim_quote: A T1 injury report cannot elevate a T3 biomechanics signal to public citation.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: T1/T3: Dimensionless tiers; Public Citation: Boolean flag for external validity.
primitives.assumptions: Epistemic quality is determined by the weakest link in the evidentiary chain (series circuit logic).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violated during heuristic blending where strong priors override weak likelihoods without explicit uncertainty quantification.

layer2.mapping: Derives the GSE veto kernel, explicitly blocking state transitions that rely on sub-threshold biomechanical proxies.
layer2.telemetry: Rate of rejected composite claims due to insufficient biomechanical tier compliance.

primitives.name: Exact Source Attribution
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Attribution precision**: Each public claim must name the exact modality and source.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Public Claim: String/Vector output; Modality: Categorical identifier; Source: URI or official registry pointer.
primitives.assumptions: Deterministic traceability is required for all generated insights to maintain system auditability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down in black-box neural network aggregations where feature importance cannot be mapped back to raw modalities.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the GSI provenance ledger, ensuring every probabilistic output carries an immutable metadata payload.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of generated insights possessing fully resolved, machine-readable source URIs.

primitives.name: Video Analytics License Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Commercial license required**: YES for any commercial video analytics platform.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: License: Binary boolean (True/False); Platform: Commercial software instance.
primitives.assumptions: Legal rights act as a hard boundary condition on the admissibility of extracted kinematic data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: System failure occurs if unlicensed community-sourced video is erroneously ingested into the T2 production pipeline.

layer2.mapping: Forms the foundational input filter for the GSE video ingestion module, halting processing if license flags are absent.
layer2.telemetry: Volume of video clips rejected at the I/O boundary due to missing commercial licensing tokens.

primitives.name: Licensing Constraint Violation
primitives.verbatim_quote: brication**: Claiming "biomechanics data indicates..." when no biomechanics data license is active is a P0 fabrication violation under Rule U5 (No Fabrication).
primitives.assumptions: Claims must be validated against active license state; absence of license implies P0 violation.

layer2.mapping: Each forbidden claim type maps to a specific modality's license requirement in GSI's probabilistic verification framework.
layer2.telemetry: Evidence item flagging upon license mismatch

primitives.name: Modality Aggregate Endpoint
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Phase 2 (post-MVP)**: Radar modality — Statcast public aggregate endpoint after legal review of commercial terms.
primitives.assumptions: Aggregate endpoints are accessible only post-legal review and MVP phase.

layer2.mapping: GSE state transition to enable radar data ingestion based on legal and temporal constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Endpoint readiness signal from legal/compliance module

primitives.name: Modal License Approval Cycle
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Phase 3+**: All remaining modalities require separate owner approval cycles.
primitives.assumptions: Each modality requires independent approval process beyond MVP.

layer2.mapping: GSI's license management system mirrors GSE's multi-modal access control logic.
layer2.telemetry: Approval cycle counter and modality-specific status flags

primitives.name: Evidence Modality Validation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Confirm all SportsScienceEvidenceItem records have a valid modality field 2.
primitives.assumptions: All evidence items must possess a defined modality for integrity.

layer2.mapping: GSE performs runtime validation of evidence modality fields during ingestion.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter window 2 introduces foundational modalities for biomechanical data capture, each governed by distinct physical principles and data acquisition protocols. Force plates measure contact dynamics through strain gauges, enabling quantification of ground reaction forces during locomotion or impact events. Radar systems exploit Doppler shifts to infer velocity and trajectory characteristics of projectiles, forming the basis of pitch tracking and batting analytics. Positional tracking relies on triangulation or inertial measurement units to reconstruct player paths, offering insights into spatial behavior and movement efficiency. Video-based computer vision applies machine learning to extract semantic meaning from raw footage, supporting tactical analysis and biomechanical evaluation. Each modality presents unique challenges in terms of data integrity, licensing requirements, and integration into broader analytical pipelines. The interplay between these modalities necessitates careful consideration of evidence tiers, access controls, and computational models that respect both physical constraints and ethical usage guidelines. Licensing restrictions such as those imposed by MLB's Statcast or OBP/Driveline underscore the need for institutional compliance and legal vetting before data ingestion. These considerations inform the design of GSI's probabilistic inference framework and GSE's situational reasoning engine, ensuring alignment with domain-specific constraints while maximizing utility for performance optimization.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 3 establishes the rigorous boundary conditions for integrating heterogeneous biomechanical and health data into a unified quantitative framework. The core mathematical challenge lies in defining a valid metric space where disparate data types—ranging from open-source pose estimation JSON (MediaPipe/OpenPose) to proprietary Hudl Sportscode outputs—can be meaningfully aggregated without violating their inherent epistemic constraints. We observe that while T3 research tools provide high-dimensional kinematic vectors, their lack of commercial licensing and standardized calibration introduces significant aleatoric uncertainty. Conversely, T1 official injury reports offer low-dimensional but extremely high-confidence categorical states. The sovereign primitive derived here, the Independent Tier Floor Constraint, mathematically enforces that the union of these sets cannot exceed the minimum fidelity of its constituents. This prevents a common statistical fallacy where a highly confident, low-frequency T1 prior (e.g., 'player is active') artificially reduces the variance of a noisy, high-frequency T3 posterior (e.g., 'subtle gait asymmetry'). By treating modality mixing as a series circuit of evidentiary gates, we ensure that the Galaxy Sports Engine only executes state transitions backed by uniformly robust telemetry. Furthermore, the requirement for exact attribution precision acts as a topological invariant, preserving the lineage of every data point through complex transformation layers. This doctrinal derivation ensures that our predictive models remain grounded in verifiable physical reality rather than spurious algorithmic correlations.

Historically, sports analytics suffered from 'black box' aggregation, blindly feeding raw pixel data into regression models. The shift toward tiered admission gates mirrors the evolution of financial market microstructure theory, where tick-level data must be cleaned and validated against official exchange timestamps before pricing derivatives. We retroactively recognize this chapter as the formalization of 'epistemic hygiene' in sports intelligence.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a theory of mind perspective, this taxonomy models the cognitive architecture of elite coaches and team physicians. These agents do not simply average data; they apply hierarchical vetoes. A coach will never alter a starting lineup based solely on a noisy computer-vision estimate of a player's hip rotation if the official medical staff has cleared them (T1 status). Our primitives emulate this human intuition by hard-coding the dominance of official participation status over inferred biomechanical fatigue. It acknowledges that opposing agents operate under similar informational hierarchies, allowing GSE to anticipate market inefficiencies arising from misaligned modality weighting.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The cross-layer veto mechanism is critical for preventing leakage between the GSI probabilistic layer and the GSE situational reasoning layer. Specifically, we must veto any attempt to use T3 biomechanical proxies to explain away T1 injury designations. If a player is officially listed as 'Out', no amount of historical pose estimation data can mathematically justify a non-zero probability of participation in the current state space. This anti-collinearity check ensures that our conformal prediction intervals do not widen artificially to accommodate contradictory evidence tiers. The veto triggers whenever a high-tier categorical fact conflicts with a low-tier continuous inference, forcing the system to default to the higher-certainty domain and flagging the discrepancy for human operator review.
